scope: Proposition I.13 (Linear rank accounting) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 192. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the following three assertions, with their permitted early or augmented logarithmic cost bounds: 1. rank preparation and conditioned sampling remove the lowest D slots of weight j, retaining positive absolute score and producing spaces with P h dim Wh ≤ D; 2. a family of recursively returned patches of rank at most d∗ can be globalized in the same patch group as in Proposition I.6; 3. transferring this fixed global patch to the parent costs at most P h dim Wh new slots, and uses an arbitrarily prescribed fixed multiplicative discount of the target density. Assume also the unconditioned base case returns rank at most d0 and permits an arbitrarily prescribed fixed density discount. Then processing an old patch with d slots returns rank at most d0 + d. For fixed s, its total multiplicative density discount can be made at most any prescribed ϵ0 > 0.
